narrative.headline: Top 50 tape skews decisively bullish — 28 of 50 mega-caps show positive institutional positioning led by mega-cap tech, healthcare, and staples accumulation.
bullish_setups: AMZN: perfect 10.0 composite — $15M call premium + $510M dark pool accumulation
NVDA: $82M in call premium (largest flow $ on the board) + $938M dark pool print, score 8.90
GOOGL/GOOG: both scoring 9.3+ with combined ~$1.17B dark pool and $14M call premium — coordinated accumulation across share classes
LLY: perfect 10.0 — $495M dark pool with clean call-side flow
TSLA: 8.49 flow with $25M call premium + $319M dark pool, blocks maxed at 10.0
CAT: cyclical tell — 8.34 flow, $527M dark pool, blocks 10.0
UNH: $8.6M call premium + $388M dark pool despite healthcare volatility
CSCO/TXN: enterprise tech quietly accumulated, both >9.2 composite with strong dark pool
bearish_setups: META: 4.16 flow score — put-heavy near-money premium, sole mega-cap tech being distributed
NFLX: weakest score at 1.98, flow 2.93 — clear put skew
WMT/COST/KO/PM: staples names getting sold on flow (2.5–3.4) even as PG/PEP get bought — selective distribution within the group
MU: 3.95 flow, put-side positioning ahead of memory cycle debate
C: 3.30 flow — banks showing bearish skew
narrative.rotation_signal: Rotation into mega-cap tech (AMZN, GOOGL, NVDA, TSLA), pharma (LLY, JNJ, MRK, UNH), and select staples (PG, PEP) — out of META, NFLX, and consumer defensives (WMT, COST, KO). Cyclicals CAT and TXN being accumulated suggests institutions are not defensively positioned despite selective staples selling.
narrative.diverging_from_industry_layer: META bearish read diverges from broadly bullish mega-cap tech complex — worth flagging vs Communication Services industry signal. WMT/COST bearish while AMZN maxes bullish suggests a specific consumer-discretionary vs traditional-retail preference not visible at the sector level.
